resources.name: The Global FoodBanking Network
resources.summary: An international directory of member food-bank organizations, useful where a direct RWN listing is not yet available.
resources.availabilityNote: This is a network directory, not a walk-in provider. Follow the member link for local access information.
resources.sourceDetail: The official global-reach page identifies member networks and countries served.

resources.accessType: Free web and mobile refill map
resources.costNote: Free water refills at listed spots
resources.name: mymizu Free Water Refill Map
resources.summary: A global map of public fountains and participating businesses that provide free drinking-water refills.
resources.availabilityNote: Some locations are community-contributed. Check recent details and ask staff before relying on a business refill point.
resources.sourceDetail: mymizu states that its free app maps more than 200,000 refill spots worldwide.

resources.costNote: Free tap-water refills at participating points
resources.name: Refill Return
resources.address: App-based refill network originating in the United Kingdom
resources.summary: A free app connecting people with public taps and participating refill locations, including a large UK network.
resources.availabilityNote: The app may prompt for an account after limited searches. Confirm that a participating location is open before travelling.
resources.sourceDetail: The official campaign page describes more than 30,000 public taps in its UK network and a broader global refill map.
resources.coverageNote: More than 30,000 UK public taps plus global refill locations.

resources.name: Covenant House
resources.costNote: All services and programs are available at no cost.
resources.address: Nationwide network covering the United States and Canada
resources.summary: Covenant House provides safe harbor and supportive services to young people ages 18 to 24 who are facing homelessness, disconnection, and exploitation. The network offers emergency overnight shelters, meals, showers, and individualized case plans to help youth achieve stability.
resources.availabilityNote: Shelters are open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. No referral is needed. Services are for young people ages 18 to 24 facing homelessness, disconnection, and exploitation.
resources.sourceKind: Official network page published by the operator
resources.sourceDetail: The official Covenant House website states that their shelters are open 24/7 for youth ages 18 to 24 and that all services and programs are available at no cost.
resources.verifiedQuote: "Our services and programs are available at no cost."
resources.coverageNote: Coverage area: Nationwide network covering the United States and Canada. The map marker is geographic context, not a single service address.

resources.name: Dress for Success
resources.costNote: Services are provided at no cost to the community.
resources.address: Global network with affiliates in multiple countries
resources.summary: Dress for Success is a global network that empowers women to achieve economic mobility. It provides professional attire, a network of support, and career development tools to women seeking employment.
resources.availabilityNote: Clients must obtain a referral to visit their local Dress for Success boutique. Services are provided through independent local affiliates.
resources.sourceKind: Official network page published by the operator
resources.sourceDetail: The official Dress for Success Austin page states that each affiliate provides all services at no cost to the community. The global site confirms it operates in multiple countries.
resources.verifiedQuote: "each affiliate provides all services at no cost to the community"
resources.coverageNote: Coverage area: Global network with affiliates in multiple countries. The map marker is geographic context, not a single service address.

resources.name: International Emergency Services
resources.costNote: The services are provided at no cost to individuals affected by disasters and conflict.
resources.summary: The Salvation Army's International Emergency Services (IES) provides critical relief, including food, water, and emergency shelter, to communities affected by disasters and conflict worldwide. The program supports local territories in disaster preparedness and response to meet immediate needs and build resilience.
resources.availabilityNote: Services are deployed in response to disasters and conflicts globally, providing immediate relief and long-term recovery support.
resources.sourceKind: Official network page published by the operator
resources.sourceDetail: The official page states that IES empowers individuals and communities by meeting immediate needs without discrimination.
resources.verifiedQuote: "meeting immediate needs and building resilience in relationship with others and without discrimination"
resources.coverageNote: Coverage area: Global disaster response network. The map marker is geographic context, not a single service address.
